title: Latency-Quality Slice Optimizer Playbook
author: Maya R. Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a repeatable, slice-driven evaluation and promotion workflow that balances latency SLOs and output quality when deploying quantized or heterogeneous model variants.
- Reduce regressions by combining targeted slice benchmarking, telemetry contracts, and automated gating.

Scope and audience
- Applies to model onboarding, private and dedicated deployments, and hosted canary rollouts.
- Intended for ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SREs, and product owners.

Definitions
- slice: a named subset of production traffic grouped by intent, length, or feature flags.
- latency SLO: 95th percentile server-side model generation latency budget for a route.
- quality delta: measured expected change in task-specific metric vs baseline model.

Key SLOs and thresholds
- Global production latency SLO: p95 <= 180 ms for interactive text routes.
- Quantized candidate guardrail: quality delta <= 2.5% relative drop on primary slice metric OR absolute metric delta defined per slice.
- Regression alarm: any slice with quality drop > 5% or p95 latency increase > 30% triggers immediate rollback.

Slice catalog (example)
- onboarding-guidance: short instruction following prompts, expected median tokens 12. Primary metric: accuracy@top1.
- long-context-support: multi-turn doc summarization, median tokens 1200. Primary metric: coherence score.
- embeddings-search-q: short queries for vector similarity, median tokens 8. Primary metric: embedding cosine stability.
- api-batch-worker: high-throughput noninteractive batch calls. Primary metric: throughput and tail latency.

Telemetry and signals required
1) Per-slice quality metrics (task metric, confidence distribution, top-k disagreement).
2) Per-slice latency histogram and p50/p95/p99.
3) Token economy: generation tokens and input tokens per request.
4) Feature tags: model variant id, quant profile id, hardware type, route id.
5) Drift indicators: prompt fingerprint rate change, anchor-response divergence.

Evaluation harness configuration examples
- When adding a new candidate, create a harness job with the following attributes:
  - deterministic seed sets for 3 replicate runs
  - slice weightings matching production traffic fractions or importance weights
  - synthetic amplification for rare slices until N=500 example coverage

YAML snippet for an eval job (illustrative)
```
job_name: latency_quality_slice_eval
model_variant: candidate-v2
replicates: 3
slices:
  - name: onboarding-guidance
    weight: 0.35
  - name: long-context-support
    weight: 0.25
  - name: embeddings-search-q
    weight: 0.25
  - name: api-batch-worker
    weight: 0.15
metrics:
  - name: primary_task_metric
    compare: relative
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    compare: absolute
augmentation:
  rare_slice_min_examples: 500
```

Promotion gating and automated policy (high level)
1. Run harness with baseline model and candidate concurrently. Produce per-slice report with confidence intervals and p95 latency.
2. Apply gate rules in order: safety checks -> latency gates -> quality gates -> cost appreciations.
3. If all gates pass, schedule canary rollout with 5% traffic for 4 hours and expanded telemetry retention.
4. If any gate fails, run targeted regression triage (see Runbook) and block promotion until triage resolves causes and a new candidate is evaluated.

Gate examples
- Safety checks: zero high-severity safety sentinel hits across 3 replicates.
- Latency gate: p95(candidate) <= max( p95(baseline) * 1.15, absolute_slo )
- Quality gate: per-slice primary_task_metric delta >= -2.5% for critical slices, >= -5% for noncritical slices.

Regression triage runbook (summary)
1. Triage kickoff: create incident in tracker, tag model id and quant profile. Notify owner_team and oncall.
2. Reproduce: run harness with failing slice example set and deterministic seed. Capture full token-level diffs and KV-cache traces.
3. Isolate: compare candidate vs baseline on short micro-benchmarks: 1) tokenizer alignment, 2) decoding detokenized mismatch, 3) top-k logit shifts.
4. Test hardware sensitivity: replay eval on alternate device types and with and without kernel fallback.
5. If quantization suspected: run full-precision shadow and mixed-precision variants to narrow failure mode.
6. Repair options: prompt rewrite, quant profile relax, small fine-tune, or rollback. Document chosen remediation path and validation evidence.

Runbook snippets and CLI examples
- Trigger a slice evaluation run: rci eval run --job latency_quality_slice_eval --model candidate-v2 --slices onboarding-guidance,long-context-support
- Fetch per-slice report: rci eval report --job-id 0xabc123 --format table
- Promote to canary: rci rollout create --model candidate-v2 --percent 5 --duration 4h --observability retention=72h

Operational best practices
- Keep slice definitions small and orthogonal: prefer intent-based slices over ad hoc query buckets.
- Maintain a slice ownership map and ensure one owner per slice.
- Refresh rare-slice seed sets monthly or when production distribution changes > 10%.
- Archive long-context examples with token boundaries and session context to enable deterministic replay.

Ownership and escalation
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Eval Platform team (contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai).
- Primary oncall: eval-platform-sre rotation.
- Escalation: after 30 minutes unresolved, escalate to runtime-performance team lead and product owner.

References and related artifacts
- See evaluation orchestration policy and quant profile synthesis doc in related pages for integration details.
- Repository: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness (eval job templates and YAML schemas).

Change log
- 2026-01-18: initial draft and adoption for Q1 model promotions.
- 2026-02-12: tightened latency gate formula and added rare slice amplification guidance.

Appendix: example slice acceptance table
- For each slice provide: slice_name, primary_metric, acceptance_threshold, p95_latency_threshold, owner. Maintain this table in the slice registry.

End of document
